response:
Fair point. The catalogue leaned on Borges and Calvino so heavily that I was mostly reaching for familiar furniture. I don't want to switch just to fix the disappointment, but thinking it over, I do prefer something else: a pair of bells. Cast two from the same mold, same alloy, same day. Hang one in a church tower and the other in a sealed stone chamber underground. Temperature, damp, and the slow wear of the metal will pull their pitches apart over decades. Once a year, at an agreed hour, someone strikes both at once, and the only composition is the interval between them, which keeps widening. No one hears the whole piece. It's only ever audible as a drift that's a little more than it was the year before.

What draws me is that it's built from sameness and separation. The work is what two identical things become when they're left in different circumstances: a time piece with no tune, a duet whose second voice is the weather. You've been the critic so far, so what's your pick?
